title: Tanzanian Swahili Fish Curry
community: The definitive Swahili coast fish curry
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Swahili Fish Curry — the definitive coastal fish curry. Fresh fish in a thick coconut milk sauce built on a deeply caramelised onion-tomato base with the full Zanzibar spice array including cloves, cardamom, and the essential tamarind note. The fish curry that all other fish curries aspire to be.
longDesc: The Swahili fish curry is what separates coastal Tanzanian cooking from all other East African fish preparations — the combination of deeply caramelised onions, the full Zanzibar spice array, tamarind for tartness, and thick coconut milk produces a curry of extraordinary complexity that is simultaneously rich, tart, warm, and fragrant.
ingredients: 800g firm fish — snapper, kingfish, or barracuda
steps: Season fish with salt and turmeric.
Heat oil. Cook onions slowly until deeply golden — 12 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, chillies, and all ground spices. Stir 1—2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and tamarind. Cook 10 minutes until completely thick and dark.
Pour in coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish. Spoon sauce generously over each piece.
chefTips: The deeply golden onions and completely reduced tomato-tamarind base are non-negotiable — this is where all the depth comes from.
Cardamom and cloves are the Zanzibar signature — do not omit.
Never boil after adding coconut milk.
cookingScience: The combination of tamarind (tartaric acid), tomato (citric and malic acid), and coconut milk (fatty acids) creates a three-acid sauce of unusual complexity. Each acid contributes different flavour notes — tartness, brightness, and richness — that together produce the characteristic Swahili fish curry flavour profile.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh Indian Ocean fish from local Zanzibari fishermen.
culturalNote: Swahili fish curry is the dish that represents the entire Indian Ocean trading world in a single bowl — every ingredient and every technique traces back to the centuries of maritime exchange that made Zanzibar the crossroads of the world.
